name: Gitea
description: Let your AI read your Gitea: find repositories, triage issues and pull requests with their comments, files, diffs and reviews, check releases and organizations, and read branches, commits and files. gitea.com or your own Gitea server, with an access token. Read-only.
instructions:
## Gitea
This connector works with Gitea through the **REST API v1** (`<your Gitea address>/api/v1`): repositories, issues with comments, labels and milestones, pull requests with their files, diffs, commits and reviews, releases, organizations with members and teams, branches, commits, the file tree and file contents. It runs against gitea.com or your own Gitea server, as the user who owns the token: the AI sees exactly what that user can see. It is **read-only**, nothing here creates, changes or deletes anything.

**Setup (about 2 minutes)**
1. In Gitea click your avatar, then **Settings**, then **Applications**. Under **Manage Access Tokens** type a name (for example "AnythingMCP") and set **Repository**, **Issue**, **Organization** and **User** to **Read** (the scopes `read:repository`, `read:issue`, `read:organization` and `read:user`). A Gitea version without token scopes gives the token the full access of its user.
2. Click **Generate Token** and copy the token right away, Gitea shows it only once. Paste only the token into `GITEA_TOKEN`: the adapter sends it as `Authorization: token <token>` and adds the word `token` itself.
3. Set `GITEA_URL` to the address you open Gitea at, for example `https://gitea.com` or `https://git.example.com`, without `/api/v1` and without a trailing slash. If Gitea runs under a sub path, keep it (`https://example.com/gitea`).

**Your own server**: a Gitea on an internal host (a private IP or an internal name) needs a self-hosted AnythingMCP on the same network, with the hostname in `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard blocks the call. Forgejo, and Codeberg which runs it, offer the same API v1 routes, so an address such as `https://codeberg.org` should work too; this adapter is written against the Gitea API.

**Repositories and numbers**: every repository is addressed by two parameters, `owner` (a user or organization name) and `repo`, the two parts of `https://host/owner/repo`. Issues and pull requests share one number sequence per repository (`index`, the 42 in `#42`). Gitea treats a pull request as an issue too: `gitea_get_issue` and `gitea_list_issue_comments` work with a pull request number for its title, labels and conversation, while `gitea_get_pull_request`, `gitea_get_pull_request_files` and `gitea_get_pull_request_diff` give the code side.

**Finding things**: `gitea_search_repositories` searches the whole instance, `gitea_list_my_repositories`, `gitea_list_organization_repositories` and `gitea_list_user_repositories` list by owner. `gitea_search_issues` searches issues and pull requests across all repositories and answers what is assigned to the token's user (`assigned`), created by them (`created`) or waits for their review (`review_requested`). Use `gitea_get_repository` first when you need the default branch.

**Reviewing a pull request**: `gitea_get_pull_request` (check `mergeable` and `merged`), then `gitea_get_pull_request_files`, `gitea_get_pull_request_diff`, `gitea_list_pull_request_commits`, `gitea_list_pull_request_reviews` and `gitea_list_issue_comments`. A diff over 200 KB is cut: open the pull request's `html_url` for the rest.

**Reading code**: `gitea_get_tree` lists files and folders at a branch, tag or commit (pass the branch name as `sha`), `gitea_get_file_content` returns a file as text (cut at 200 KB), `gitea_list_branches`, `gitea_list_commits` and `gitea_get_commit` show the history.

**Releases**: `gitea_get_latest_release` answers what the current version is, `gitea_list_releases` and `gitea_get_release_by_tag` show release notes and attached files.

**Pagination**: list tools take `page` (from 1) and `limit`. A server answers 30 items per page by default and at most 50 (its `MAX_RESPONSE_ITEMS`), so ask for the next page instead of a bigger limit. A list is returned under `data` (the repository search already does), together with `_headers` carrying `x-total-count` and `link`, and `_pagination` with `nextCursor`, the next page number. `_pagination` is missing on the last page. Comments and `gitea_get_tree` have their own paging, see their descriptions.

**Errors**: 401 means the token is wrong, expired or deleted, or `GITEA_URL` points at another server. 403 means the token lacks a scope this call needs (Gitea names it in the message), for example `read:issue` for issues or `read:organization` for organizations. 404 means the repository, issue or file does not exist or the user cannot see it: Gitea answers 404 for private resources it hides. 422 names a missing or invalid field.

**Out of scope here**: creating or editing issues, comments, pull requests, releases, branches and files, merging or approving, Actions runs and workflows, packages, wikis, notifications, webhooks, deploy keys and administration.

GITEA_URL.label: Gitea address
GITEA_URL.help: The address you open Gitea at, for example https://gitea.com or https://git.example.com, without /api/v1 and without a trailing slash. Keep a sub path if Gitea runs under one (https://example.com/gitea).
GITEA_URL.patternMessage: Use the server address, e.g. https://gitea.com or https://git.example.com, without /api/v1 and without a trailing slash.

GITEA_TOKEN.label: Access token
GITEA_TOKEN.help: Gitea, avatar, Settings, Applications, Manage Access Tokens, Generate Token, with Read for Repository, Issue, Organization and User. Gitea shows the token only once.
GITEA_TOKEN.patternMessage: Paste only the token, without spaces or the word token or Bearer in front.

verifyHints.401: Gitea refused the token: it is wrong, expired or deleted. Create a new one under Settings, Applications, and check that GITEA_URL points at the server that issued it.
verifyHints.403: The token lacks a scope this call needs: read:user for this check, read:repository, read:issue and read:organization for the tools. Create a token with Read on Repository, Issue, Organization and User.
verifyHints.404: Gitea found nothing at this address. Check GITEA_URL (for example https://gitea.com, without /api/v1, with the sub path if Gitea runs under one).

prerequisites: An account on gitea.com or on your own Gitea server, and an access token with Read permission for Repository, Issue, Organization and User. About 2 minutes.

tools.name: gitea_get_current_user
tools.description: Get the Gitea user the token belongs to: id, login, full_name, email, is_admin and html_url. A quick check that the token and the instance address work.

tools.name: gitea_search_repositories
tools.description: Search the repositories the token can see on the whole instance by keyword, topic, type or archived state: full_name, description, default_branch, stars_count, forks_count, open_issues_count, private, archived, updated_at and html_url. The list is under `data`. For one owner's repositories use gitea_list_organization_repositories or gitea_list_user_repositories.

q.description: Keyword matched against repository names (and descriptions when includeDesc is true).

topic.description: Match the keyword against repository topics only.

includeDesc.description: Also search the keyword in repository descriptions.

is_private.description: true for private repositories only, false for public ones only. Leave out for both.

archived.description: true for archived repositories only, false to leave them out. Leave out for both.

mode.description: Kind of repository: fork, source, mirror or collaborative.

sort.description: alpha, created, updated, size, git_size, lfs_size, stars, forks or id (default alpha).

order.description: asc or desc (default asc). Ignored without sort.

page.description: Page number, from 1. When _pagination is in the answer there is a next page: call again with page set to _pagination.nextCursor. It is missing on the last page.

limit.description: Results per page. The server default is usually 30 and its maximum usually 50 (the administrator sets both), so ask for further pages instead of a bigger limit.

tools.name: gitea_list_my_repositories
tools.description: List the repositories owned by the token's user, with full_name, description, default_branch, private, archived, stars_count, open_issues_count, updated_at and html_url. Repositories of an organization are not included: use gitea_list_organization_repositories for those.

page.description: Page number, from 1. When _pagination is in the answer there is a next page: call again with page set to _pagination.nextCursor. It is missing on the last page.

limit.description: Results per page. The server default is usually 30 and its maximum usually 50 (the administrator sets both), so ask for further pages instead of a bigger limit.

tools.name: gitea_get_repository
tools.description: Get one repository: description, default_branch, private, archived, fork, empty, size, stars_count, forks_count, open_issues_count, open_pr_counter, release_counter, the token user's permissions, clone_url and html_url. Use it to learn the default branch before reading files or commits.

owner.description: Owner of the repository: a user or organization name, the first part of the repository address (https://host/OWNER/repo).

repo.description: Repository name, the second part of the repository address (https://host/owner/REPO).

tools.name: gitea_list_issues
tools.description: List a repository's issues with filters: number, title, state, labels, assignees, milestone, comments count, created_at, updated_at and html_url. Gitea treats pull requests as issues too, so type defaults to issues here; set it to pulls to list pull requests with the same filters (gitea_list_pull_requests has the pull request specific ones).

repo.description: Repository name, the second part of the repository address (https://host/owner/REPO).

milestones.description: Comma-separated milestone names or ids. Issues in any of them match.

q.description: Text searched in titles and descriptions.

created_by.description: Only items created by this username.

assigned_by.description: Only items assigned to this username.

mentioned_by.description: Only items that mention this username.

before.description: Only items updated before this time, RFC 3339.

tools.description: Search issues and pull requests across every repository the token's user can see, or narrow to the ones assigned to, created by, mentioning or awaiting review from the token's user (assigned, created, mentioned, review_requested, reviewed). Each result names its repository. Use it for questions like what is assigned to me or which pull requests wait for my review.

owner.description: Owner of the repository: a user or organization name, the first part of the repository address (https://host/OWNER/repo).

repo.description: Repository name, the second part of the repository address (https://host/owner/REPO).

filepath.description: Path of the file inside the repository, slashes included, e.g. src/main.go. A name with # or ? in it is not supported.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit SHA. Leave out for the default branch; give it explicitly when a top-level folder has the same name as a branch.
